MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  June 1, 2009

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 5:00
p.m., on June 1, 2009 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on May 27, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Ledesma

CLOSED SESSION

The following expressed concern with ongoing construction at 26992 La Paja and asked the City
Council to direct the homeowner to eliminate the access gate on Payaso Lane and to rebuild the

City Council Minutes  1  June 1, 2009
 walls and planter areas that were previously there:  Christine Saracino, M.V. and Richard
Cordova, M.V.

CS1. Labor Negotiations--The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are
  the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.
CS2. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One matter of Existing Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is City of Mission
  Viejo v. CUSD, Case No. 00180049; Companion Case, Rancho Santa Margarita v.
  CUSD, Case No. 00207543.
CS3. Conference with Legal Counsel--Initiation of Litigation. Pursuant to Subdivision (c)
  of Government Code Section 54956.9. Three Cases Under Consideration.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council is still working on item CS1, and will
recess back to Closed Session at the conclusion of tonight's open session. At that time the
Council will also address items CS2 and CS3.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Certificate of Appreciation given by City of Mission Viejo to AARP Tax Aid
  Program Coordinator Glen Jerpseth

  Mayor Ury presented the Certificate of Appreciation to Glen Jerpseth.

P2.  Recognize the 20th Anniversary of the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior
  Center

  Mayor Ury presented the Proclamation to Nancy Herrmann, Community and Senior
  Center Administrator.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following expressed concern with construction activities at 26992 La Paja and Mrs. Saracino
presented the City Clerk with a Request for Municipal Action related to the access gate on

City Council Minutes  2  June 1, 2009
 Payaso Lane: Richard Cordova, M.V.; Dr. Michael Hersh, M.V.; Ann Cordova, M.V.; Roberto
Saracino, M.V.; and Christine Saracino, M.V.

Greg Bonano, Project Manager for construction at 26992 La Paja, M.V.: provided a construction
update and stated that he is ready to clean the project up and complete it as soon as possible.

Harry Lenczyk, M.V. stated that he is worried about the City’s fiscal policies and expressed
concern with the cost of expanding or enhancing current facilities.

Les Sykes, M.V.: discussed the Community Services Commissioners’ recent visit to the Shea
Therapeutic Riding Center in San Juan Capistrano. He had the honor of presenting rosettes and
trophies to the disabled riders for their skills obtained in the program. After the ceremony,
several attendees and caregivers expressed their sincere thanks to the City of Mission Viejo for
continued support of the program.

Susan Sellers, M.V.: presented a petition containing the signatures of 1,040 individuals who are
interested in a dog park in Mission Viejo. She stated that it is a win-win situation for dog
owners, businesses within the City, and a dog park would increase home values. Ms. Sellers
requested that the City consider revising the criteria for the size of a dog park and suggested that
a smaller facility would be sufficient.

The following expressed their support for a dog park in Mission Viejo: Joey Sellers, M.V.; Gil
Buck, M.V.; Suzi Scallon, M.V.; Hailey Buck, M.V.; Corissa Sellers, M.V.; Janie Salazar,
M.V.; Ivy Melton, M.V.; Ronda Emondson, M.V.; Alex Polen, M.V.; and Don Langston, M.V.

Tina Bach, M.V.: expressed concern with the City’s finances and stated that the Nadadores
should have paid for the decking at the Marguerite Aquatics complex and the City is subsidizing
the Nadadores with over $100,000 a year.

The following spoke in opposition to investing money in a dog park during financially difficult
times: John Connolly, M.V.

The following submitted written comments in favor of a dog park: Tonya and Enrique Iribarne,
M.V.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 8 through 19 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve
the Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  3  June 1, 2009
 AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the City Council Meeting of May 18, 2009, as presented.

6.  2009 Fourth of July Community Street Faire

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by the Mission Viejo Activities
  Committee authorizing the annual Mission Viejo Fourth of July Community Street Faire
  on Saturday, July 4, 2009.

7.  2009 Residential Resurfacing (CIP 838)

  Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $1,167,000 to Hardy & Harper, Inc.,
  for the subject project.

City Council Minutes  4  June 1, 2009
 20.  Mission Viejo Library Technical Services Outsourcing

  Approved the agreement with Baker & Taylor (B&T) in an amount not to exceed
  $50,000 per year for fiscal years 2009-10 and 2010-11 for the provision of electronic
  selection lists, electronic ordering, acquisitions, cataloging, and physical processing of
  library materials.

21.  Purchase of Additional Disk Space for the Backup System

  Approved a purchase order to GovPlace for the purchase of additional disk space for the
  Data Domain backup system in an amount not to exceed $59,866.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

22.  Waste Disposal Agreement between the County of Orange and the City of Mission
  Viejo

  Ron Pierre, Deputy Director, County of Orange: outlined the proposed agreement and by
  way of a PowerPoint presentation, he provided answers to questions that the Council had
  posed at the May 18, 2009, City Council Meeting.

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Ledesma,
  to approve the Waste Disposal Agreement with the County of Orange for the period July
  1, 2010, through June 30, 2020.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

Council Member Schlicht indicated that she is opposed to approving these contracts for another
two years because she feels that a bid process would allow the City to do the work cheaper.

City Council Minutes  5  June 1, 2009
 Tina Bach, M.V.: expressed opposition to the contract renewals without going out to bid. She
requested that the City agendaize the creation of a standing Committee to look at the City’s
contracts and any proposed renewals.

Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to approve items 8 through

RECESS

At the hour of 7:21 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:28
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

23.  Roundabout Intersections Committee Report

City Council Minutes  8  June 1, 2009
   Council Member Schlicht announced that she is withdrawing and postponing her report
  for two weeks.

  Robert Bruchmann, M.V.: expressed concern with the discussions at the Roundabout
  Intersections Committee meetings and stated that the consultant, Scott Ritchie, has
  already indicated that Oso/Marguerite would not be a good location for a roundabout, nor
  did Mr. Ritchie ever state that the public would love a roundabout.

  Ken Forest: stated that the fence at the Baja Finisterra housing tract is in disrepair and
  this proposal and staff’s will delay their repair project. He asked why this study wasn’t
  done earlier and he requested that the City get on with the widening project.

  Janet Alexander, M.V.: discussed her visit to the fire station situated 240 yards north of
  the intersection at Oso and Marguerite. The firefighters told her there is no way that fire
  trucks and emergency vehicles could navigate a roundabout at that intersection. Ms.
  Alexander stated that it has been disturbing to watch City Council meetings lately as one
  Council Member calls the others derogatory names and shows a lack of civility and
  character.

  Chief Scott Brown, Orange County Fire Authority: stated that response times are the
  most critical element of the fire department’s ability to respond in an emergency. He
  expressed serious concerns with the idea of a roundabout at Oso and Marguerite and the
  potential impact to response times during peak traffic flows.

  By consensus, the City Council Members agreed to address item 29 simultaneously with
  item 23.

29.  Roundabout Intersections Staff Report

  Tina Bach, M.V.: announced that contrary to popular belief, we do not need to widen
  roads to accomodate traffic. By doing this, home values will diminish and we will be a
  community divided and dissected by freeways.

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report and indicated that he wanted the
  City Council to have the same information that has been provided to the Roundabout
  Committee over the past few months.

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to
  (1) reject the recommended action (item #23) to authorize the issuance of a purchase
  order to Roundabouts and Traffic Engineering (RTE) in the amount of $19,990 for the

City Council Minutes  9  June 1, 2009
   preparation of a roundabout feasibility concept plan for the intersection of Oso Parkway
  and Marguerite Parkway and (2) receive and file the report for item #29.

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Mayor Ury, to move the
  previous question.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

  On roll call, said MAIN motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

24.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

25.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the
  Foothill/Eastern TCA but there are two upcoming meetings for which he will have
  reports at the next Council meeting.

26.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ledesma presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

27.  Oso/Marguerite Intersection Improvements (CIP 844)

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion was made by Mayor Pro Tem MacLean, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to

City Council Minutes  10  June 1, 2009
   approve the bid specifications and authorize staff to advertise for construction bids for the
  subject project.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Ledesma, MacLean, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

  Council Member Schlicht stated for the record that she voted against this item because
  she believes there is a better option. After spending close to $8 million that intersection
  will have a service level rating of F-E. She believes that with a roundabout, the
  Oso/Marguerite intersection would have a service level of A-B at half the price.

28.  2009-2011 Budget Workshop Schedule

  City Manager Wilberg stated that staff's schedule calls for delivery of the proposed 2009-
  11 Budget at June 15th Council Meeting. Staff suggests a budget workshop shortly
  thereafter, preferably the week of June 22nd, with adoption of the final Budget at the July
  20th City Council Meeting.

  By consensus, the City Council selected Monday, June 22nd for the Budget Workshop.

City Attorney's Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

30.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City
  Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley added a few comments to the OCFA report she provided for item 24.
She referred to a statement made by a member of the audience earlier this evening regarding the
money spent on the Crown Valley beautification efforts. The resident indicated that she would
have preferred that the landscaping monies had been used to build a dog park, however Council
Member Kelley noted that the all of the money spent on the Crown Valley Parkway widening

City Council Minutes  11  June 1, 2009
 project came from other resources such as Ladera Ranch, development impact fees, federal
dollars, and grant funding.

City Manager Wilberg confirmed that the landscaping was provided through a grant and that the
money spent on Crown Valley Parkway could not be used in other areas of the City.

Council Member Kelley commended staff on a wonderful Memorial Day event. She noted that it
was very well attended and she was pleased that the City had an opportunity to acknowledge
those who have died in service to our country. She reminded residents of the Relay for Life this
weekend at Saddleback College. The event begins at 10 a.m. on Saturday, June 6 and ends at 10
a.m. on Sunday, June 7, 2009. Council Member Kelley encouraged residents to attend and stated
that it’s not too late to join a team. Interested parties can visit www.mvrelay.org for more
information. She also reminded residents to mark their calendars for the DAWG Walk on June
27, 2009, at Oso Viejo Park. Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance this past week at
the City’s Environmental Fair. The City hosted over 540 3rd grade students who learned about
the environment, recycling, composting and what they can do to help make a difference. The
City of Mission Viejo provides this event through grant funding and Council Member Kelley
stated that the children and their teachers are very appreciative of the program. Finally, Council
Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of June is
citizenship.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma discussed the concept of a roundabout at Oso and Marguerite. He
stated that a big factor in our future is the traffic that will be generated as a result of the
development to our east. He noted that the County approved the housing plan without an
extension of the 241 Toll Road and as far as they are concerned, a toll road extension is not
necessary. Council Member Ledesma commended City staff for once again organizing a very
inspiring Memorial Day Service. It is wonderful that the City does so much to honor our
veterans, specifically those that have made the ultimate sacrifice for us. He announced that he
had the pleasure of attending the ribbon cutting ceremony at the new Sonic restaurant and it was
especially exciting to see that project come to fruition since he was the listing agent on the
property.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht mentioned that she too attended the Memorial Day ceremony. It is
always moving and it was a special honor to participate this year as a City Council Member. She
discussed her recent visits to TK Burgers and Gandolfo’s and she thanked them for choosing

City Council Minutes  12  June 1, 2009
 Mission Viejo. Council Member Schlicht invited residents to attend a Town Hall Meeting with
Sheriff Hutchens and the Mission Viejo Police Chief on June 9th from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the
City Council Chamber. She asked staff to discuss the Crown Valley Parkway widening and
stated that the City Council was told, on March 2, 2009, that the project would be officially
complete on May 29th.

City Manager Wilberg stated that the road widening was complete on April 2, 2009, and the City
is still working with the hospital to finalize the artwork display.

Council Member Schlicht discussed a letter she received from a homeowner who lost their pet to
a coyote in broad daylight. She asked what the City is doing to control the coyote population.

City Manager Wilberg stated that we periodically have increased incidents with coyotes and he
will ask the Animal Services Manager to provide a report to the City Council on the subject.

Council Member Schlicht noted that she has received inquiries about her Council portrait and her
bio for the web site. She stated that she will get that squared away as her time becomes more
available but it has not been a priority and she personally believes that the Council Members’
faces should not be displayed in every building.

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Mayor Pro Tem MacLean announced that for the 20th straight year since its incorporation in
1988, the City has been recognized for excellence in financial reporting by the Government
Finance Officers Association of the United States and Canada. The City has been honored with
a Certificate of Achievement - the highest recognition - for its 2008 Comprehensive Annual
Financial Report. This award is based on a government agency’s demonstration of a
constructive spirit of full disclosure. Mayor Pro Tem MacLean stated that the City prides itself
on transparency and openness and the ability for its residents to know exactly how the money is
spent to improve the quality of life. Mayor Pro Tem Maclean stated that he is proud to be a part
of this organization and he complemented Administrative Services Director Irwin Bornstein and
his staff on their great work.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury reminded residents that they can submit budget ideas by email to
budget@cityofmissionviejo.org. He noted that all of the budget meetings will be televised or
they can be viewed on the City’s web site. Mayor Ury congratulated Council Member Kelley on
all that she has done for the Relay for Life and he announced that he is looking forward to

City Council Minutes  13  June 1, 2009
 attending that event this weekend. He also discussed his attendance at the Sonic grand opening
and stated that he and his family had a fantastic time and he is looking forward to Sonic’s
success in town. Mayor Ury noted that the Memorial Day ceremony was very moving and the
speaker gave everybody the charge to make sure they understand the sacrifice that military
personnel have made for our country and to make sure that the younger generation recognizes
the same. Mayor Ury expressed his sincere thanks to those who have served.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 8:44 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 10:20 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that there was nothing to report from Closed Session.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:22 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, June 15, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.
